title: Burrow‐Based Monitoring of Chinese Pangolin (Manis pentadactyla) Reveals Importance of Core Natural Habitat in Hong Kong中華穿山甲 (Manis pentadactyla)洞穴監測揭示香港內陸郊野地帶的重要性
content:
Relatively little is known about the distribution or habitat requirements of Hong Kong's population of the Chinese pangolin. Between 2018 and 2021 we searched for pangolin burrows and deployed camera traps on the burrows. We then analyzed habitat suitability at multiple scales to determine the factors that are key in driving pangolin distributions in Hong Kong. The most important factor was distance to coast, reflecting the importance of core natural habitat for the species. Our results emphasize core natural habitat requirements for the Chinese pangolin in Hong Kong and point to opportunities in the management and monitoring of the species.


ABSTRACT

The Chinese pangolin (Manis pentadactyla) is a Critically Endangered species with elusive habits that challenge monitoring efforts. In Hong Kong and for much of its distribution, basic questions on the population biology, distribution, and habitat associations of M. pentadactyla have not been fully investigated. We developed a burrow-based monitoring approach relying on reconnaissance walks across grids coupled with landscape-scale modeling based on remote sensing data to fill these knowledge gaps for the species. From 2018 to 2021 we detected a total of 248 burrows across sites in Hong Kong, with active usage of a subset of these verified through camera trapping. The burrow-level analysis revealed that burrows tended to be further away from the coast and at higher elevations than random. Burrows were also found in grasslands, shrublands, and mature forest in roughly equal proportions. For the grid-level analysis, we found burrows were more numerous further away from the coast, when areas had an east-facing aspect, and with lower proportions of shrubland and urbanization. Both scales of the analysis identified distance to coast as the most important factor suggesting that core natural habitats and undisturbed/protected areas are key for pangolin persistence in Hong Kong. We found no evidence of human hunting for pangolins but dogs were recorded at an active burrow. The rare and elusive nature of M. pentadactyla can complicate monitoring efforts but our results here demonstrate how burrow-based approaches, particularly when leveraged in landscape analysis and remote sensing (and LiDAR especially), can be used to provide key conservation and wildlife management insights.

摘要

中華穿山甲(Manis pentadactyla)是一種極度瀕危的物種。其行蹤隱匿的習性使到監察此物種普遍面臨挑戰。不論在香港或其他分布地區, 有關此物種的族群生物學、分布和棲息地關聯性等的研究十分有限。我們通過結合實地考察以及遙感數據分析, 建立一套以洞穴分布為基礎的監測方法, 以填補對於中華穿山甲的知識缺口。研究團隊在2018年至2021年期間於香港一共發現248個中華穿山甲的洞穴, 並以紅外線監測相機確認部分洞穴近期曾被穿山甲使用。洞穴層級的數據模型顯示, 中華穿山甲的洞穴普遍處於離海岸較遠和海拔較高的地方。此外, 它們均可在草原、灌木和成熟樹林生境內找到, 佔比大致相同。展示洞穴密度的網格層級的數據模型則顯示, 離海岸較遠、地勢朝向東方、灌木覆蓋率較低以及都市化程度較低的地方, 洞穴數量較多。兩項分析模型皆指出離岸距離是決定中華穿山甲洞穴分布的最重要因素, 顯示內陸郊野地帶以及未受干擾/受保護地區對於中華穿山甲在香港的存續至關重要。另外, 我們未有觀察到非法捕獵中華穿山甲的跡象, 但曾於一處洞穴前記錄到野狗出沒。面對中華穿山甲行蹤隱匿, 令其難以監察的問題, 此研究提供了一套結合實地洞穴考察、景觀分析與遙感數據(尤其是光學雷達(LiDAR))的監測方法, 有助更有效地保育和管理此瀕危物種。
